lesson.title: Searching 2D Lists
lesson.driving_question: How can a program search rows for one matching key and respond when no record matches?
lesson.primary_concept_family: Finding a record by a text key and reporting a not-found route
lesson.concept_budget: Compose known loops, selection, indexing and a Boolean flag for one linear record search; no new search API is used.
misconceptions: The flag starts False before the search.
A match changes the flag inside the loop.
The not-found message is checked after all rows.
The search compares the key field rather than the whole row.
lesson.progression_note: Completes the Grade 8 2D-list strand and prepares the same work to be decomposed into functions.

primm.prompt: Recall how a for loop visits each row, how lower() normalises text, and how a Boolean flag records whether an event occurred.
Use Chess. Trace target and found through all three rows, then decide whether the not-found message appears.
Run with Chess and then Music. Confirm one path displays a member count and the other displays Club not found.

questions: Why is the target normalised before it is compared with stored record names?
Why must found start as False before the search loop?
What goes wrong if the not-found message is placed inside the loop?
If you enter code, what message appears, and does Club not found. appear?

When [club][0] matches [target], ask for a new member count and store it in [new_members]. Update [club][1], then display "Updated:" followed by the changed row. Test "Chess" and 20; display "Updated: ['chess', 20]". Test "Music"; display "Club not found."

Store ["orbit", 120], ["harbour", 96] and ["forest", 144] in [books]. Ask for a title and store its lower-case value in [target]. Use a for loop to compare [target] with each title. Display "Pages:" followed by the page count when a title matches. Display "Book not found." only after every row has been checked and no match was found. Test "Harbour"; display "Pages: 96". Test "Music"; display "Book not found."
Repair the key-field index, use assignment when a match is found, and test the not-found flag after the loop.

programs.challenge2:
clubs = [["art", 12], ["chess", 18], ["code", 15]]
target = input("Club to update: ")
target = target.lower()
found = False
for club in clubs:
    if club[0] == target:
        new_members = int(input("New members: "))
        club[1] = new_members
        print("Updated:", club)
        found = True
if found == False:
    print("Club not found.")
